subject.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue

question: Should an internally queued durable wake remain deliverable after the canonical session key has been reset to a new session generation, or must it be fenced to the generation that owned the wake?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically implementable, but they encode different user-visible session ownership and stale-context guarantees; the existing queue deliberately treats `agentTurn` and `systemEvent` continuations differently, so code inspection alone cannot determine the intended durable-wake policy.

options.title: Fence to source generation
options.body: Record the expected session id on the durable wake queue entry and skip or supersede it after a reset, preventing stale wake context from entering a new conversation.

options.title: Survive session resets
options.body: Keep the session-key-scoped `systemEvent` behavior, but document it as an intentional durable ownership transfer and add live proof that the post-reset experience is safe and understandable.

options.title: Defer the handoff
options.body: Keep wake inspection and persisted attempts but postpone automatic queue handoff until the reset and ownership contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Fence to source generation
recommendation.body: Record the expected session id on the durable wake queue entry and skip or supersede it after a reset, preventing stale wake context from entering a new conversation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing session delivery queue and its generation-fencing behavior, so they are the strongest history-backed owner for this policy decision.
